key_points: Residual collateral perfusion pressure is crucial during cerebral function monitoring.
Primary closure in arterial repair is speedy but may lead to recurrent stenosis.
Patch closure ensures complete plaque removal but requires longer time.
Eversion CEA is attempted to avoid patch closure.
Hospitals with fewer annual CEAs have poorer results unless large volumes are handled.
Surgical risk increases with age; particular attention needed for patients over 75.
surgical_outcomes: ACAS study reports a 1.5% morbidity and mortality rate for CEA.
In NASCET and ECST studies, older patients faced higher risks.
In SPACE trial, lower benefits noted for patients over 75 from CEA.
gender_factors: Women have higher operative risk and less favorable outcomes than men.
demographic_factors: Older age is linked with higher perioperative risk.
Race-based differences in CEA outcomes are unclear due to study limitations.
